name: Successful/Failed Logons
purpose: Profiles account creation, attempted logons, and account usage through the core Security-log authentication event IDs.
key_fields: Event ID 4648 — logon using explicit credentials (runas)
Event ID 4672 — account logon with superuser (administrator) rights
Event ID 4720 — an account was created
normal_baseline: 4624/4634 pairs align with expected work-hours usage for known accounts; 4625 failures are isolated and infrequent; 4672/superuser logons correspond to known administrative activity; 4720 account-creation events align with change-managed onboarding.
anomalies: A burst of 4625 failures against one or many accounts in a short window, consistent with password spraying or brute force
4648 (explicit credential logon / runas) using an account that shouldn't have a reason to authenticate from that host
4672 superuser logon for an account outside the expected administrator list
4720 account creation outside a documented change window, especially followed shortly by a 4672 admin-rights logon for the same account
anti_forensic_notes: The Security log can be cleared (itself logged as Event ID 1102) or rotated out under high logon volume; correlate with a SIEM/forwarder for retention beyond local log rotation limits.
interpretation: Use 4624/4625 as the anchor pair for any account-usage timeline, then layer 4648 (explicit creds) and 4672 (elevated rights) on top to distinguish a routine logon from a privilege-escalation-relevant one. Cross-reference with `logon-event-types` for what each 4624 Logon Type code actually means (console vs network vs RDP vs service, etc.) before drawing conclusions from the raw event alone.
